domain: Updates the animation selection of every populated entry in a 4-slot AnimationObject array on an AnimationSetupState, driven by a packed flags byte (high bit + a 7-bit selector), but only when the 7-bit selector differs from the state's cached value.
behavior: high_bit = flags & 0x80; flags &= 0x7f (the low 7 bits become the animation-table selector)
no-op (returns 0 immediately) when state->field36 already equals the masked selector

otherwise, for each of up to state->count entries: skips a null entry or one whose 'table' word is 0; looks up metadata via Func_08185000(entry->id); skips entries whose selector is out of range against metadata->animation_count

on a valid entry: writes draw_kind from metadata, selects entry->current from a per-metadata s32 table indexed by the selector (entry->table[selector], NOT a direct metadata->animation copy the way the template sibling does it), sets a 0x10 marker byte, and -- only when the high bit of flags was clear -- zeroes two more entry fields
for entry index 0 only, also copies metadata->adjust_x/adjust_y into two state fields
stores the new selector into state->field36 before returning 0

bounded_search.reason: Iteratively fixed: (1) computing high_bit/flags in-place from the same parameter register instead of separate locals, which removed an extra r9 spill; (2) reading entry->table twice (matching reference's redundant reload) instead of caching it in a pointer local; (3) correcting metadata field offsets so the index==0 copy reads adjust_x/adjust_y at their real offsets 6/7 instead of an accidentally-duplicated pair of fields at 8/9. Also tried rewriting the loop as an explicit rotated do-while to see if it would stop the compiler hoisting state->count out of the loop condition -- it produced byte-identical output to the plain for-loop, so it was reverted for readability.

remaining: 166 vs 154 bytes (12 over). The largest known gap: this candidate's compiler reads state->count ONCE before the loop and reuses that value for every iteration's bound check, while reference re-reads it through a cached pointer on every iteration (visible as 'mov r2,r8; ldrb r3,[r2,#0]; cmp r1,r3' inside the loop back-edge in the real assembly). Neither a for-loop nor an equivalent rotated do-while over 'state->count' reproduced that repeated-read shape, so this is either a genuine compiler loop-invariant-hoisting difference this candidate hasn't triggered the right source form for, or a residual outside manual respelling's reach. A second, smaller gap is a 4-byte stack-frame difference (sub sp,#12 vs reference's #8) whose cause was not isolated.
notes: 2026-08-31: adopted byte-exact. The reference is a rotated pre-tested loop with one shared increment/backedge, not the earlier ordinary for-loop or an unconditional do/while. Preserving that source layout and compiling this owner with the shipped -fno-strength-reduce flag prevents induction-pointer conversion and restores the indexed state->entries[index] load. Naming selected_animation before the independent draw-kind copy fixes the final four scheduling differences. Final score: 154/154 bytes, zero differing halfwords, equal branch topology.

Struct field names (field20, field02, field34, field35, field36, table) are placeholder offsets, not evidence-backed names; only draw_kind, id, marker-position, and the adjust_x/adjust_y copy are corroborated against the template's AnimationMetadata layout.

Sibling 0800bbc0 (also assigned) shares the same 0800b7c0 template family and the same AnimationObject/AnimationMetadata table but implements a different operation (allocating a new object into a free table slot rather than updating an existing one's animation selection); its dossier documents that owner separately, including the same struct-uncertainty caveat.

Recovered only from retained owner assembly, the already-adopted initialize_objects.c template, and the approved compiler.
